key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks and DeepONets can approximate difficult infinity- and p-Laplace PDEs across large p values, offering a scalable alternative to traditional mesh-based solvers.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for high-dimensional nonlinear PDE simulation, especially in 3D where conventional discretization becomes expensive and slow.
method: Train PINNs to solve infinity and p-Laplace problems directly from the PDE residuals.
Use DeepONets as surrogates for the parametric p-Poisson problem.
Test across 2D and 3D domains with p ranging from 2 to 1000.
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical experiments comparing neural solvers against conventional methods, alongside conditional convergence results for PINNs and a universal approximation result for DeepONets.
watch_item: Performance may depend on problem setup and the stated convergence guarantees are conditional, so robustness and training stability should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Deep-Learning Solvers and Surrogates for Infinity and p-Laplace Problems
